newsitem.title: PORTUGAL: FOCUS - Portugal earns $775 million from Cimpor sale.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS - Portugal earns $775 million from Cimpor sale.

text.p: Portugal earned $775 million from the privatisation of a 45 percent stake in the country's biggest cement producer, Cimpor-Cimentos de Portugal, on Tuesday, officials said.

"The value of the sale was about 120 billion escudos ($775 million)," Fernando Teixeira Santos, Under-Secretary for Finance, told reporters at a special session at the Lisbon bourse to announce details of the sale.
"After Portugal Telecom, we have now seen another operation marked by strong demand and great success," he said.

The Socialist government, which expects to earn around 450 billion escudos ($2.9 billion) from privatisations this year, sold off a second 22 percent tranche of Portugal Telecom in a comfortably oversubscribed sale in June.
Demand for shares in the privatisation of Cimpor exceeded the available supply more than four times, officials said.
Cimpor president Antonio Sousa Gomes said Portugal would exercise a "green shoe' option due to the strong demand.
The "green shoe', totalling more than 2.8 million shares, can be drawn on to provide additional shares to institutional investors if demand is very heavy.
Analysts said the strong demand was due to confidence in the financial health of Cimpor, a climate of falling interest rates and good medium-term growth prospects for the company.
Cimpor said last month that full 1996 net profit would be at least double the 11.6 billion escudos ($75 million) earned in the first six months of the year.
It will benefit from house- and road-building programmes and construction for the 1998 Expo World Fair in Lisbon.
The cash-rich company has said it plans to acquire foreign cement producers in coming years.
"The company is taking steps to ensure a steady flow of income beyond the year 2000," said Mark Howard, analyst with Lloyds Bank Fund Managers in Cascais, near Lisbon.
The previous Social Democrat government sold a 20 percent stake in Cimpor. The government now has a 35 percent holding.
It floated the 45 percent stake partly through a book-building process and partly through a public offer to sell (OPV). The privatisation price was 3,170 escudos per share.

Analysts had expected the price to be between 3,150 and 3,250 escudos, below the 3,278 at which it closed bourse trading on Monday. Cimpor shares stood at 3,265 escudos, down 13, in high volume of 213,226 shares in early afternoon trading on Tuesday.
The privatisation price is either that of the direct sale or a recent average of the share price plus five percent, whichever is lower.
Both the direct sale and OPV were more than four times oversubscribed, officials said.

They said total demand for 74.095 million shares comfortably outstripped the available 17.76 million shares in the direct sale, which comprised 3.9 million shares sold in Portugal and 13.86 million sold internationally.
The government earned around 69.8 billion escudos ($451 million) from the direct sale, officials said.
Total demand for 78.8 million shares exceeded the available 17.2 million shares in the OPV, officials said.
The government earned 50.2 billion escudos ($324 million) from the OPV, they added.
